entities.statement: Investigate whether a general-purpose LLM, executed locally and contextualized only with process knowledge and normal operation, can detect the emergence of an abnormal condition in a multivariate industrial system under a fault-zero-shot protocol.

Can a general-purpose LLM, without fault-specific training and contextualized only with knowledge of the process and its normal operation, detect in a fault-zero-shot setting the emergence of an abnormal condition in a multivariate industrial system? The Tennessee Eastman Process with IDV(13) is the focal experimental case.

entities.label: H1 — Zero-shot detection capability
entities.statement: A general-purpose LLM contextualized only with process knowledge and normal operation can detect an abnormal condition caused by a previously unseen fault without fault-specific training.

entities.label: H2 — Temporal accumulation of evidence
entities.statement: The LLM's anomaly-detection capability increases as multivariate fault evidence accumulates across causal temporal windows, producing an observable transition from NORMAL or EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT to ANOMALY after the true fault onset.

entities.label: H3 — Multivariate evidence coherence
entities.statement: When the LLM indicates an anomaly, the variables and trends cited in its justification correspond to changes actually observable in the system, even without prior knowledge of the IDV(13) identity.

entities.label: DPCA with T-squared and SPE/Q
entities.role: Independent statistical reference for detection timing and contributing variables; not ground truth and not an input to the LLM in the primary condition

entities.label: Open general-purpose LLM executed locally
requirements: The primary condition must use no fault-specific fine-tuning or training.
The primary condition may expose process semantics and normal-operation reference information.
The primary condition must not expose labeled IDV(13) examples, the IDV(13) description, hidden simulator fault flags, or DPCA outputs.
Model, quantization, prompt, parameters and hashes must be recorded.
RAM, VRAM, latency, tokens and outbound traffic must be measured.
The model must support an evidence-insufficient response.

scope.primary_task: Fault-zero-shot detection of abnormality rather than nominal identification of IDV(13)
scope.protocol: Progressive causal windows without access to future observations
conditions: Fault-blind local LLM with process knowledge, normal-operation reference and structured temporal representation, without DPCA output
Local LLM assisted by DPCA evidence, pending scope decision as a secondary condition
metrics: Detection delay from true fault onset

entities.statement: A reproducible protocol for evaluating fault-zero-shot anomaly detection by general-purpose local LLMs on multivariate industrial temporal data, including normal-reference context, structured causal windows, alarm and abstention rules, evidence-coherence evaluation and verifiable local execution.
